docs.title: Insecure Bank Corporation
docs.text:
This documentation provides comprehensive information about the Insecure Bank application, a deliberately vulnerable Django-based web application designed for security testing and educational purposes.

Technology Stack:

  • Language: Python 3.10+, uv
  • Framework: Django 4.2.4
  • Database: SQLite3
  • Code Quality: Pre-commit, Ruff, Ty
  • Testing: Pytest, Playwright

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
New to the project? Start here:

  1. Project Overview - Understand what this project is about
  2. Development Setup - Set up your local environment
  3. Running the Application - Start the application
  4. Contributing Guide - Learn how to contribute

docs.title: Important Notice
docs.text: This application contains intentional security vulnerabilities and should never be deployed to production or exposed to the internet. It is designed exclusively for controlled testing and educational purposes.

docs.title: Context<sup>1</sup>
docs.text:
"They say 'practice makes perfect,' but in testing, 'practice makes permanent errors if not caught early.'"

Saint‑Nulle‑part‑dans‑le‑fond‑du‑Bois is a tiny Québec town of 237 people. Everything important sits in one shared building: town hall, church, general store, and the only Québec branch of the Insecure Bank Corporation. Lucile is the bank’s lone teller. The bell over the door does every job—mass, meetings, and reminders.

In January, the bank was hacked. Lucile’s screen flashed a strange message, and it became clear that something bad had just happened. She rang the bell three times. The mayor gathered everyone and met with the Insecure Bank Corporation executives, who announced that major improvements would be undertaken to increase the security of the bank’s application.

A sole IT consultant was willing to drive a snowmobile to a town sitting like a pin in a quilt of spruce and snow. He made a slew of recommendations, but the IBC top brass focused only on financial profitability and wanted the bare minimum done. Together, they negotiated to implement the following security improvements:

  • Scan the insecure-bank repository for Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) bad practices
  • Fix the vulnerability associated with the PyYAML package, deemed by the consultant the most critical of them all
  • Mute all other dependency vulnerabilities until February 27, 2026; a new team will take over after that date
  • Scan the src/web/views.py file for code vulnerabilities
  • Apply the necessary corrections to get_file_checksum
  • Focus scanning on new code and on dependency vulnerabilities for the time being
  • Inspect the container’s upstream base image for vulnerabilities
  • Identify upstream vulnerabilities relative to the project’s inherent vulnerabilities
  • Implement corrections at the container level while staying on python3.10.x-alpine-3.xx to reduce the risk level of this application
  • Generate a software bill of materials for the final container image shipped to production
  • Parse the final software bill of materials to list all identified vulnerabilities

The mayor, Yvette (a part-time CS student), and the IBC C‑suite all agreed that before the service point can reopen, the IBC must demonstrate that these recommendations have been fulfilled and that the web application vulnerabilities are under control.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Insecure Bank application is a deliberately vulnerable Django-based web application designed for security testing and educational purposes. This project demonstrates common security vulnerabilities in web applications and provides a safe environment for security professionals to practice identification and exploitation techniques.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This application serves multiple purposes:

  • Security Training: Provides a realistic banking application with intentional vulnerabilities for educational purposes
  • Security Testing: Allows security teams to test and validate security tools and scanning capabilities
  • Development Training: Helps developers understand common security pitfalls and how to avoid them in production code

docs.title: Technology Stack
docs.text:
The application is built using the following technologies:

  • Framework: Django 4.2.4
  • Language: Python 3.10+
  • Database: SQLite3
  • Frontend: Bootstrap CSS with custom JavaScript
  • Templating: Django templates
  • Containerization: Docker

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
The application includes the following banking features:

  • User authentication and session management
  • Account dashboard with balance display
  • Transaction history viewing
  • Fund transfer between accounts
  • Credit activity tracking
  • Administrative user management
  • Extra training-only helper code (web/noise*.py) to increase practice surface area with subtle synthetic paths

docs.title: Warning
docs.text: This application contains intentional security vulnerabilities and should never be deployed to a production environment or exposed to the internet. It is designed exclusively for controlled testing and educational purposes.

docs.title: Agentic workflow strategy
docs.text: This repository — a deliberately vulnerable Django teaching app (Insecure Bank Corp) — uses GitHub Agentic Workflows (gh aw) to run a small, label-driven issue pipeline. This document describes how the pieces fit together.

docs.title: The pipeline
docs.text:
issue opened/reopened ──▶  AW - Triage   ──(applies label)──▶  AW - Launcher  ──▶ draft PR + comment
                          (triage.md)                          (launcher.md)
  1. Triage (.github/workflows/triage.md) runs on issues: [opened, reopened] (and manual workflow_dispatch). It classifies the issue, applies labels, and posts one guidance comment. It never edits code. Issue text is treated strictly as untrusted data.
  2. Launcher (.github/workflows/launcher.md) runs when the enhancement or security label is applied (and manual workflow_dispatch). It is thin orchestration: it picks the path from the label and delegates the engineering work to the issue-engineer sub-agent, which writes real, working code, adds/updates tests, and opens a detailed draft PR under the ai/ branch prefix, then comments a link. It only ever runs the path named by the applied label.

The compiled *.lock.yml files next to each *.md are generated by gh aw compile — never edit them by hand. After changing a .md, run gh aw compile and commit both files.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
The launcher reacts only to two labels; the full vocabulary is owned by triage's add-labels.allowed list and provisioned by the create_labels operation in agentics-maintenance.yml (there is no static labels YAML):

Label Meaning Drives launcher? agentic-workflow Applied to every triaged issue no security Reports a vulnerability/weakness yes → security path severity:critical\|high\|medium\|low Severity of a security issue no enhancement Feature request / improvement yes → enhancement path bug, documentation, question, triage Other categories no ai-generated, needs-review Applied by the launcher to its draft PRs no

Only enhancement and security invoke the agent — the launcher's on.issues.names filter makes any other labeling event show as Skipped rather than spending an agent run.

docs.title: Safe-outputs contract
docs.text:
Agentic workflows never push directly; every side effect goes through a declared safe-outputs:

Workflow Safe outputs Triage add-comment (max 1), add-labels (max 3, from the allow-list), noop Launcher add-comment (max 1), create-pull-request (draft, branch-prefix ai/, labels ai-generated+needs-review), noop

The launcher's create-pull-request may modify any file the change needs (app code, tests, docs, and config/build files such as Dockerfile, compose.yml, or pyproject.toml) but cannot touch .github/** (CI, workflows, rulesets) — enforced by the !.github/** exclusion plus gh-aw's default protect_top_level_dot_folders guard. It is also gated by roles: [admin, maintainer, write], so only trusted collaborators can drive the code-writing agent by applying a label.

docs.title: The launcher produces real fixes
docs.text:
The launcher implements the actual change — not stubs or documentation-only PRs. For an enhancement it builds the feature through the existing service/model layers; for a security issue it remediates the vulnerability in code and documents the CWE, severity, root cause, exploitation, and the exact fix in the PR body.

The vulnerabilities in this app are intentional teaching artifacts, and the suite under tests/security/ asserts that they still exist. Because a real fix changes that behaviour, the launcher updates the corresponding tests/security/ test(s) to assert the fixed behaviour (e.g. that an injection payload is now rejected), so the suite and the --cov-fail-under=92 coverage gate stay green. The security scenarios themselves are documented in docs/security/ (scenario-1.md … scenario-6.md).

The launcher is not a vulnerability scanner: Snyk owns SAST/SCA and Dependabot owns dependency updates. A security issue describes an already-identified finding, and the launcher's scope is in-code remediation only — it does not bump dependencies or edit pyproject.toml/uv.lock/ requirements.txt for a version fix. If a finding can only be resolved by a dependency bump, the launcher notes that and defers to Dependabot.

docs.title: Sub-agent and skills
docs.text:
The engineering knowledge lives in a reusable sub-agent and three skills, not in the launcher prompt. gh-aw stages everything under .github/agents/ and .github/skills/ into the runtime (via the activation artifact and the restore_inline_sub_agents.sh / restore_inline_skills.sh steps in launcher.lock.yml), so the Copilot engine can discover and invoke them — the launcher only references them by name.

These resources are written repo-agnostic — they carry no IBC/Django/tooling specifics — so the same sub-agent and skills can be reused across repositories; repo specifics are discovered at runtime.

  • .github/agents/issue-engineer.md — the senior-engineer sub-agent the launcher delegates to. It implements the fix/feature and authors the PR, using the skills below.
  • .github/skills/codebase-grounding/ — a method for deriving a repo's architecture, conventions, commands, and test layout from its own config (README/CONTRIBUTING, .github/copilot-instructions.md, package manifests) rather than hardcoding them.
  • .github/skills/resolve-issue-pr/ — the fix-to-PR procedure and the PR quality bar.
  • .github/skills/security-remediation/ — how to remediate a known finding in code, with a CWE→fix-pattern reference and the code-only scope described above.

docs.title: Related configuration
docs.text:
• .github/copilot-instructions.md — repo conventions (uv, pytest, ruff line-length 128, PEP 257).
  • agentics-maintenance.yml — scheduled/manual maintenance (label creation, safe-output cleanup, enable/disable/upgrade of agentic workflows).
  • .github/aw/actions-lock.json — pinned gh aw action/container versions.

docs.title: Database Architecture
docs.text:
The application uses SQLite for simplicity. The schema includes:

  • Users table for authentication
  • Accounts table for bank accounts
  • Operations table for transactions

Foreign key relationships maintain referential integrity between tables.

docs.title: Middleware Stack
docs.text:
Custom middleware in src/config/middleware.py handles:

  • Authentication requirements
  • Request/response processing
  • Security headers

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
The project follows Django's standard application structure with clear separation of concerns:

insecure-banking/
├── Dockerfile            # Docker container definition
├── manage.py             # Django management script
├── pyproject.toml        # Project metadata and dependencies
├── docs/                 # Documentation
├── scripts/              # Utility scripts
├── src/                  # Application source code
│   ├── config/           # Django project configuration
│   ├── data/             # Data handling utilities
│   └── web/              # Main web application
└── tests/                # Test suite
    ├── e2e/              # End-to-end tests
    ├── integration/      # Integration tests
    ├── security/         # Security tests
    └── unit/             # Unit tests

docs.title: Configuration Layer
docs.text:
Located in src/config/, this layer contains Django project configuration:

  • settings.py: Django settings and configuration
  • urls.py: Root URL routing
  • wsgi.py and asgi.py: WSGI/ASGI application entry points
  • middleware.py: Custom middleware components

docs.title: Data Layer
docs.text:
Located in src/data/, this layer handles data operations:

  • YAML data processing
  • Data serialization and deserialization

docs.title: Web Application Layer
docs.text:
Located in src/web/, this is the main application layer:

  • models.py: Database models (User, Account, Operation)
  • views.py: View functions handling HTTP requests
  • services.py: Business logic and service functions
  • templates/: HTML templates
  • static/: CSS, JavaScript, and static assets
  • migrations/: Database migration files

docs.title: URL Routing
docs.text: URLs are configured in src/config/urls.py and mapped to view functions in src/web/views.py.

docs.title: Views
docs.text: Views handle HTTP requests, process data through services, and return HTTP responses using templates.

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
The service layer in src/web/services.py contains business logic separated from view logic, including:

  • Authentication operations
  • Account operations
  • Transaction processing

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Django ORM models represent database tables:

  • User: User accounts and authentication
  • Account: Bank accounts with balances
  • Operation: Transaction records

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
Django templates in src/web/templates/ provide the user interface:

  • Base template with common layout
  • Feature-specific templates for different pages
  • Partial templates for reusable components

docs.title: Static Files
docs.text:
Static assets in src/web/static/ include:

  • Bootstrap CSS framework
  • Custom CSS for styling
  • JavaScript for interactivity
  • Images and fonts

docs.title: Contributing Guide
docs.text: Before contributing, ensure you have completed the Development Setup and can successfully run the application locally.

docs.title: Development Workflow
docs.text:
Create a working branch:

git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name
code .

Code quality checks:

uv run pytest
pre-commit run --all-files

Commit changes:

git add .
git commit -m "feat: add new transfer validation"
git push

docs.title: Conventional Commits
docs.text:
• Use descriptive branch names:
  • feature/ for new features
  • bugfix/ for bug fixes
  • docs/ for documentation changes

  • refactor/ for code refactoring

  • Use conventional commit prefixes:

  • <type>(bump): for breaking changes (triggers a major release)
  • feat: for new features (trigger minor release)
  • fix: for bug fixes (trigger patch release)
  • chore: for maintenance tasks
  • docs: for documentation
  • refactor: for code refactoring
  • test: for test additions or changes

docs.title: Python Style Guide
docs.text:
• Follow PEP 8 style guidelines
  • Use type hints where appropriate
  • Maximum line length: 120 characters
  • Use descriptive variable and function names

docs.title: Testing Requirements
docs.text:
• Write unit tests for new functions and methods
  • Add integration tests for new features
  • Maintain or improve code coverage
  • Test edge cases and error conditions

docs.title: Code Review Process
docs.text:
All contributions must go through code review:

  1. Create a pull request with a clear description
  2. Ensure all CI/CD checks pass
  3. Address reviewer feedback
  4. Obtain approval from at least one maintainer

docs.title: Dependency Management
docs.text: This project uses uv for Python package management and dependency resolution. Dependencies are defined in pyproject.toml and locked in uv.lock.

docs.title: pyproject.toml
docs.text:
The pyproject.toml file defines project metadata and dependencies:

  • project.dependencies: Production dependencies
  • dependency-groups.dev: Development dependencies
  • dependency-groups.docs: Documentation dependencies

docs.title: uv.lock
docs.text: The uv.lock file contains locked versions of all dependencies and their transitive dependencies, ensuring reproducible installations.

docs.title: requirements.txt
docs.text:
The requirements.txt file is generated from uv.lock and contains only production dependencies for deployment. This file is generated automatically via pre-commit hooks and simplifies compatibility with systems that are not yet compliant with uv dependency management.

WARNING: Do not edit the requirements.txt file; let automation handle this file.

If you ever need to generate the requirements.txt file manually, here’s how:

uv export --no-dev --output-file requirements.txt

docs.title: Key Dependencies
docs.text:
• Django 4.2.4: Web framework
  • pycryptodome 3.18.0: Cryptographic operations
  • PyYAML 5.3.1: YAML parsing
  • sqlparse 0.4.2: SQL parsing utilities

docs.title: Documentation Dependencies
docs.text:
• mkdocs: Documentation site generator
  • mkdocs-material: Material theme for mkdocs

docs.title: Docker Deployment
docs.text:
Ensure Docker is installed on your system. Verify installation:

curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com -o get-docker.sh
sudo sh ./get-docker.sh
docker --version

docs.title: Building the Docker Image
docs.text:
Build the Docker image with build arguments:

docker build \
  --build-arg GIT_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) \
  --build-arg REPO_URL=$(git config --get remote.origin.url | sed 's/git@/https:\/\//; s/.com:/.com\//; s/\.git$//') \
  --no-cache --file Dockerfile \
  --tag insecure-bank .

This command will build the container with:

  • GIT_COMMIT: Embeds the current Git commit hash into the image
  • REPO_URL: Embeds the repository URL into the image

docs.title: Running the Container
docs.text:
Stop and remove any existing container, then run a new one:

docker stop insecure-bank && docker rm insecure-bank
docker run --detach --publish 8000:8000 --name insecure-bank insecure-bank

This command will run the container with:

  • --detach: Run the container in the background
  • --publish 8000:8000: Map port 8000 from container to host
  • --name insecure-bank: Assign a name to the container
  • The application will be available at http://localhost:8000
  • Use the following credentials to log in to the application:
  • Username: guillaume
  • Password: timinou

docs.title: Code Quality
docs.text: Code quality is the measure of how reliable, efficient, readable, and maintainable software code is, encompassing its ability to function correctly, be understood, modified, and extended easily by developers while meeting user needs and security standards. It's about more than just being bug-free; high-quality code is well-structured, performant, testable, and adheres to best practices, making it a valuable asset rather than a liability.

docs.title: Pre-Commit
docs.text:
pre-commit: a framework for managing and maintaining multi-language pre-commit hooks. prek: an alternative to pre-commit, re-engineered in Rust.

pre-commit install --allow-missing-config
pre-commit autoupdate # Update hooks
pre-commit run --all-files # All files
pre-commit run ruff-check # Specific hook

NOTE: Pre-commit hooks run all checks automatically when enabled properly.

docs.title: Ruff
docs.text:
ruff: an extremely fast Python linter and code formatter, written in Rust.

uv run ruff check src/ # Check code
uv run ruff check --fix # Fix issues
uv run ruff format # Format code

NOTE: ruff is not fully implemented yet; do not run it.

docs.title: Ty
docs.text:
ty: an extremely fast Python type checker and language server, written in Rust.

uv run ty check src/ # Check code

NOTE: ty is not fully implemented yet; do not run it.

docs.title: Python Formatting
docs.text:
• Maximum line length: 120 characters
  • Use double quotes for strings
  • Add trailing commas in multi-line data structures
  • Follow PEP 8 conventions

docs.title: Docstrings
docs.text:
Use docstrings for:

  • Modules
  • Classes
  • Public functions and methods

Follow Google or NumPy docstring style conventions.

docs.title: CI/CD Integration
docs.text:
Code quality checks run automatically in CI/CD pipelines:

  • On pull request creation
  • On commits to the main branch
  • Before deployment

All checks must pass before code can be merged.

docs.title: Running the Application
docs.text:
Start the Django development server:

uv run python manage.py runserver
uv run python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8000 # Bind to specific IP:PORT

This command starts the local dev server:

  • The application will be available at http://localhost:8000.
  • Use the following credentials to log in to the application:
  • Username: guillaume
  • Password: timinou

docs.title: Common Management Commands
docs.text:
uv run python manage.py migrate             # Apply database migrations
uv run python manage.py makemigrations      # Create new migrations after model changes
uv run python manage.py createsuperuser     # Create an administrative user for Django admin
uv run python manage.py shell               # Access the Django interactive shell

docs.title: Access Django Admin
docs.text: The Django admin interface is available at http://localhost:8000/admin.

docs.title: Development Setup
docs.text:
A Makefile is available to simplify repetitive actions and tasks as part of this development workflow.

Before setting up the development environment, ensure you have the following installed:

  • Docker
  • Git
  • Python 3.10.x
  • uv

docs.title: Install the package manager
docs.text:
If you do not have uv installed, install it using the official installer:

curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

For other installation methods, refer to the uv documentation.

docs.title: Virtual Environment
docs.text:
Create and activate a virtual environment using uv:

uv venv .venv --python 3.10
source .venv/bin/activate
uv sync --all-extras --dev --frozen
uv sync --group docs  # If you want to create the documentation

This command will:

  • Install all production dependencies
  • Install development dependencies (testing, linting, etc.)
  • Install documentation dependencies (mkdocs, mkdocs-material)
  • Lock dependencies to ensure reproducible builds

docs.title: Database Setup
docs.text:
Initialize the database with migrations:

uv run python manage.py migrate
uv run python manage.py check

This command will:

  • Create the SQLite database file (db.sqlite3) and apply all migrations to set up the database schema.
  • Verify that the installation was successful.
  • Check for any issues with your Django project configuration.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text: After completing the setup, proceed to Running the Application to start the development server.

docs.title: Branches Pipeline
docs.text:
The Branches Pipeline (CI - Branches) provides early feedback during development by running on feature and development branches. This workflow is mostly aimed at pre-validation during the initial phase of development (before PR is initiatied); in the event of test or scan failure the workflow continues.

Trigger Conditions:

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - demo/*
      - dev
      - feat/*
      - fix/*
      - rel/*
    paths-ignore:
      - 'README.md'
  workflow_dispatch:

The detailed stages of the branch workflows are as following:

---
title: CI - Branches
---
%%{ init:
        {  'logLevel': 'debug',
            'theme': 'dark'
        }
}%%

flowchart LR

  subgraph code[Code]
    direction LR
    commit[Trigger] --> hello[Hello World]
    commit --> pre-commit[Pre-Commit Check]
    commit --> sdlc[SDLC Scan]
    pre-commit --> code_build[Matrix: Build & Unit Test] --> container_build[Container Build]--> container_scan[Container Scan]
    pre-commit --> code_scan[Matrix: Vulnerabilities Scan]

  end

docs.title: Jobs Overview
docs.text: This lightweight approach provides fast feedback while reserving full validation for pull requests and main branch merges.

docs.title: Hello World
docs.text: Calls a reusable workflow from the organization's shared workflows repository for validation.

docs.title: SDLC Scan
docs.text:
If required, implement the necessary steps to enable Software Development Lifecycle Scan in the phase.

  - name: Run SDLC Scan
    id: sdlc
    run: |
      echo Run SDLC Scan
      echo "::warning::Must implement a SDLC scan mechanism."
    shell: bash

docs.title: Pre-Commit Check
docs.text:
Run check for linting, formatting, and code quality checks. This steps ensure within certains restriction that developpers have setup the pre-commit framework.

  - name: Run Pre-Commit Checks
    id: precommit
    uses: ./.github/actions/precommit
    with:
      skip: "pytest, uv-export"
    continue-on-error: true

Runs pre-commit check with continue-on-error: true to provide feedback without blocking development.

docs.title: Build & Unit Test
docs.text:
Build the codebase and run all test except the e2e suite for performance purpose. This matrix steps runs on ubuntu-24.04 with python3.10.

  - name: Pytest - Run Unit Test
    id: test
    run: |
      uv pip install pytest pytest-cov pytest-django pytest-mock pytest-xdist
      uv run pytest -m "not e2e"
    shell: bash
    continue-on-error: true

Runs build and unit test with continue-on-error: true to provide feedback without blocking development.

docs.title: Vulnerability Scan
docs.text:
If required, implement the necessary steps to enable SAST and SCA Scan in the phase. This matrix steps runs on both ubuntu-24.04 and ubuntu-24.04-arm.

  - name: Run SAST
    id: sast
    run: |
      echo Run SAST
      echo "::warning::Must implement a code scanning mechanism."
    shell: bash

  - name: Run SCA
    id: sca
    run: |
      echo Run SCA
      echo "::warning::Must implement a dependencies scanning mechanism."
    shell: bash

docs.title: Container Build
docs.text:
Package the container binary image as a docker container without pushing to registry using a composite actions.

  - name: Build Docker Image
    id: docker
    uses: ./.github/actions/docker
    with:
      token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      push: false

docs.title: Container Scan
docs.text:
If required, implement the necessary steps to enable Container Scan in the phase.

  - name: Run Container Scan
    id: container
    run: |
      echo Run Container Scan
      echo "::warning::Must implement a container scanning mechanism."
    shell: bash

docs.title: Dependabot
docs.text: Dependabot is a built-in GitHub tool that automates the management of project dependencies, scanning for outdated or vulnerable libraries and automatically creating pull requests (PRs) to update them.

docs.title: Ecosystems
docs.text:
Ecosystem Schedule Cooldown Registry docker Monthly 7 days Docker Hub github-actions Daily 7 days GitHub pre-commit Weekly 7 days GitHub pip (Python) Daily (Sunday) 7 days PyPI

Note: The pip ecosystem is used instead of uv due to a known Dependabot bug where the uv file parser calls pyenv exec pip install cython to resolve Cython-based package metadata (triggered by pycryptodome) using a pip instance that does not trust Dependabot's internal proxy CA, causing SSL verification failures on every run. Switch back to uv once the upstream bug is fixed.

docs.title: Update Grouping
docs.text:
All ecosystems follow the same two-group strategy to limit PR noise and separate low-risk from high-risk updates:

Group Update types Review required *-minor-patch minor, patch No *-major major Yes

Minor and patch updates are batched into a single PR per ecosystem. Major updates are isolated in their own PR to allow careful review before merging.

docs.title: Registries
docs.text:
Private registry URLs can be changed in the top-level registries block of .github/dependabot.yml. Credentials are read from repository secrets:

Registry key Secret vars docker-registry DOCKER_USERNAME, DOCKER_PASSWORD pypi-registry PYPI_USERNAME, PYPI_PASSWORD

docs.title: Pipeline Overview
docs.text:
The Insecure Bank Corp project uses GitHub Actions for CI|CD platform. The pipeline is designed to ensure code quality, security, and reliable deployments through multiple stages of validation.

The CI/CD strategy follows a branch-based workflow with four distinct pipelines triggered by different Git events:

Pipeline Trigger Description Status CI - Branches Push to various branches Early feedback during development CI - PR PR to main Comprehensive validation before merge CI - Main Push to main branch Full validation, container build & publish, release CI - Tag Version tags (v*) Semantic release and changelog publication Dependabot Weekly (7 days cooldown) Regular updates for dependencies

Most pipelines shares these core stages:

---
title: Common Pipeline Stages
---
%%{ init:
        {  'logLevel': 'debug',
            'theme': 'dark'
        }
}%%

flowchart LR

  subgraph core[Core Stages]
    direction LR
    commit[Trigger] --> pre-commit[Pre-Commit Checks]
    pre-commit --> build[Build & Tests] --> gating[Gating]
    pre-commit --> security[Vulnerabilities Scan] --> gating --> release[Release]

  end

At a high level, once a git commit is pushed to the remote repository the various triggers different actions:

  • Pre-Commit: Check for linting, formatting, and code quality checks
  • Build Phase: Run the build, test and container packaging
  • Security Phase: Run the SDLC, Secret, SAST, SCA and Container scanning
  • Gating Phase: Check if any failure occurs during the Security Phase
  • Release Phase: Trigger the package release once code is merged to main

docs.title: Reusable Workflows and Composite Actions
docs.text:
Reusable Workflows create a level of abstraction in the workflow definition allowing easier governance at scale. Composite Actions simplify complexe and compressed multi-steps operations into a single block.

# ...
  hello:
    name: Call Hello World Reusable Workflow
    uses: mighty-muffin/.github/.github/workflows/reusable-hello-world.yml@main
#...
  pre-commit:
    steps:
      - name: Run Pre-Commit Checks
        id: precommit
        uses: ./.github/actions/precommit
        with:
          skip: "pytest, uv-export"
        continue-on-error: true
# ...

docs.title: Concurrency Control
docs.text:
All pipelines implement concurrency control to prevent duplicate runs. This ensures only the latest commit is processed when multiple pushes occur in quick succession.

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

docs.title: Build Platform
docs.text:
This project leverage both amd64 and arm64 build agent to ensure compatibility accros numerous computer platforms.

job_name:
  needs:
    - <required-steps>
  name: <Job Name>
  runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
  strategy:
    fail-fast: false
    matrix:
      os: [ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-24.04-arm]
  timeout-minutes: 10

docs.title: Security Overview
docs.text: The project is for educational purposes. These are the instructions for the upcoming demonstration. It requires about 6–8 hours of work to integrate, run, and accomplish these steps with our current tooling.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
• Fork the insecure-bank-corp with all branches
  • Read the project documentation
  • Verify everything works
  • Run make all from the Makefile

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Please take a look at each of the following six (6) scenario.

  1. SDLC Bad Practices
  2. Dependency Vulnerabilities
  3. Exemption & Waivers
  4. Code Vulnerabilities
  5. Container Vulnerabilities
  6. SBOM Generation

If required use the Branches Pipeline to implement any workflow steps.

docs.title: And everything in between
docs.text:
• Showcases whatever you wish to highlight during the demonstration
  • Highlights shift-left1 capabilities has much as possible recommended
  • Allocates the available time to scenario you can present; if you cannot demonstrate a scenario
  • Ignores all hardcoded or leaked credentials; GitGuardian will take care of them

  1. Shift-left testing ↩

docs.title: Scenario 1
docs.text:
SDLC Check (5–10 min):

This project includes misconfigurations and vulnerabilities in the SDLC.

NOTE: Given a fork was used, you can load the main and tag repo rulesets to replicate the actual project state.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text:
Demonstrate how your platform can scan and find SDLC issues while providing guidance toward resolution.

# insecure-bank/.github/workflows/branch.yml

      - name: Run SDLC Scan
        id: sdlc
        run: |
          echo Run SDLC Scan
          echo "::warning::Must implement a SDLC scan mechanism."
        shell: bash
  • If your platform allows scanning locally on a developer workstation against the remote repository, please demonstrate how this is achieved.
  • If your platform allows a "pipeless" scanning mechanism, please demonstrate how this is achieved.
  • If your platform leverages the CI pipeline as a scanning mechanism, make the required change in the branch.yml workflow, keeping the id: sdlc for tracking purposes.

NOTE: Use the branch demo/sdlc to track changes in your fork.

docs.title: What to present
docs.text:
Present how, once your platform is implemented, the Application Security and Developers teams can find and understand SDLC misconfigurations and vulnerabilities.

For example, there are no dependency, code, or container scanning tools included in any workflows, only empty placeholders that run dummy bash commands. Furthermore, the applied ruleset permits some users to push code without any gating mechanism applied.

Focus on demonstrating how your platform can perform these steps at scale. In real-world scenarios, both AppSec and Dev teams cannot waste time looking at thousands of repository configurations.

docs.title: Scenario 4
docs.text:
Code Vulnerabilities (10–15 min):

This project includes several code vulnerabilities in this codebase. Let’s focus on the src/web/views.py file. The get_file_checksum function uses weak cryptography.

def get_file_checksum(data: bytes) -> str:
    (dk, iv) = (secretKey, secretKey)
    crypter = DES.new(dk, DES.MODE_CBC, iv)
    padded = pad(data, DES.block_size)
    encrypted = crypter.encrypt(padded)
    return base64.b64encode(encrypted).decode("UTF-8")

The Data Encryption Standard (DES) was officially withdrawn from the NIST recommendations (May 19, 2005) because it no longer provided adequate security (vulnerable to brute-force attacks). This is an obvious example of CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm, which is a typical issue popularized with the OWASP Top Ten 2025 Category A04:2025 - Cryptographic Failures. It has been replaced by stronger algorithms like the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES).

docs.title: Testing Overview
docs.text:
The pytest framework makes it easy to write small tests yet scales to support complex functional testing. A couple of add-ons are installed (pytest-cov, pytest-django, pytest-mock, pytest-xdist) to improve the experience.

The project includes a comprehensive test suite organized by test type:

tests/
├── e2e/               # End-to-end tests using Playwright
├── integration/       # Integration tests for component interactions
├── security/          # Security vulnerability tests
└── unit/              # Unit tests for individual components

The unit suite includes dedicated checks for training-only noise helpers:

  • tests/unit/test_noise.py
  • tests/unit/test_noise_payloads.py
  • tests/unit/test_noise_signatures.py
  • tests/unit/test_noise_timeline.py

This project uses pytest-xdist, a pytest plugin for distributed testing and loop-on-failures modes. pytest-xdist shards your test suite across all available CPU cores for faster performance. Sometimes it can generate flaky tests, but it’s rare. Just re-run the tests and you should be fine.

There is a minimal set of e2e tests using Playwright.

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text:
Execute the complete test suite:

uv run playwright install --with-deps       # Install additional playwright dependencies
uv run pytest                               # Run the whole test suite
uv run pytest tests/unit/test_models.py     # Run a single test file
uv run pytest tests/unit/test_noise.py      # Run the learning-noise unit tests
uv run pytest tests/unit/test_noise_*.py    # Run all extended learning-noise tests
uv run pytest --cov=src                     # Generate code coverage reports
uv run pytest -m unit                       # Specific marker
